claims.text: Differences between ORAL Surveillance and STAR-RA in baseline cardiovascular risk enrichment and study design (randomized trial versus observational database analysis) complicate cross-study interpretation; furthermore, the indexed abstracts cannot establish full numerical effect sizes or determine whether residual confounding explains differences.
claims.reason: Cross-source interpretation needs research and regulatory or label evidence.

answer: ORAL Surveillance was an open-label, randomized noninferiority postauthorization trial comparing tofacitinib (5 mg or 10 mg twice daily) with a TNF inhibitor in patients aged 50 years or older with active rheumatoid arthritis despite methotrexate and at least one cardiovascular risk factor. In ORAL Surveillance, the combined tofacitinib doses failed to demonstrate noninferiority compared with a TNF inhibitor for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and cancers. STAR-RA was an observational comparative study using healthcare claims databases (Optum, MarketScan, Medicare) that created a routine-care real-world evidence cohort and an RCT-duplicate cohort mimicking ORAL Surveillance inclusion and exclusion criteria. In STAR-RA routine-care patients, investigators found no evidence of increased cardiovascular risk with tofacitinib versus TNF inhibitors, although an increased risk that was not statistically significant was noted among patients with cardiovascular risk factors. In a September 1, 2021 communication, the FDA concluded based on the completed randomized safety trial that tofacitinib carries an increased risk of serious heart-related events, stroke, cancer, blood clots, and death compared with TNF blockers in rheumatoid arthritis. The November 10, 2026 prescribing information for Xeljanz describes RA Safety Study 1 (NCT02092467) as evaluating patients aged 50 and older with at least one cardiovascular risk factor, noting higher observed incidence rates of MACE and mortality compared to TNF blockers.
limitations: Do the full texts of ORAL Surveillance and STAR-RA provide specific hazard ratios and subgroup analyses to evaluate residual confounding?
